findings.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:133 — When a slot falls on a date-override day and inside its window, `return true` exits before the `busy.every` check, so existing bookings, calendar events and buffers during override hours are ignored and the slot can be double-booked.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:123 — With several override ranges on the same day (e.g. 09-11 and 14-16), every slot is outside at least one range, so `find` returns truthy and every slot on that day is rejected.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:110 — Overrides are matched to slots by the UTC calendar date, not the organizer's local date, so a PST evening override (e.g. Jan 11 5-8PM = Jan 12 UTC) wipes normal Jan 12 slots and drops override slots that fall after UTC midnight.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:139 — The new working-hours check returns "outside" if the slot is outside ANY entry for that weekday, so split schedules (lunch breaks) and UTC-midnight-split entries (e.g. Sydney 9-5) reject valid slots.

packages/lib/slots.ts:219 — The override conversion keeps only hour*60+minute after adding the offset, dropping the day, so a window that crosses the invitee's midnight gets endTime < startTime, or lands 24h off (e.g. IST 00:30 override shown to a UTC invitee on the next day); checkIfIsAvailable then rejects those slots, so the override is silently lost.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:110 — The left side uses local-mode `dayjs(date.start).format()` (server TZ) while `slotStartTime` is UTC, so matching only works when the server runs in UTC; tests pass in a UTC CI but break on non-UTC hosts.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:114 — ===` compares two distinct Dayjs objects and is always false, so the "unavailable all day" (start==end) override branch is dead code and a slot starting exactly at that instant is treated as available.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:123 — The bounds check only rejects slotStart > override end, so a slot starting exactly at the override end or running past it is accepted as inside the override (and then skips the busy check).
packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:142 — end` is computed from slotStartTime instead of the slot end time, so a slot that runs past the end of working hours is never caught.

apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts:797 — toHaveTimeSlots only walks the actual slots, so a subset or a truncated result passes; the new test also has no busy booking inside the override, no multi-range override and no invitee behind the organizer, so it misses the P0/P1 bugs.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:107 — The organizer offset is computed at the fake-UTC wall-clock instant rather than the real instant, so it can be off by an hour on DST transition days.
packages/lib/slots.ts:212 — override.timeZone` is optional; when undefined, `.tz(undefined)` falls back to the server's local timezone, silently giving the wrong offset for callers that don't set it.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:133 — When any date override matches the slot's day, checkIfIsAvailable returns true before the busy check, so bookings and calendar conflicts are ignored on override days (double-booking).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:106 — dateOverrides.find rejects a slot as soon as one same-day override excludes it, so days with several override ranges (e.g. 9-12 and 14-17) lose valid slots in every range except the first.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:139 — workingHours.find rejects a slot if any entry for that UTC day excludes it, so multiple ranges per day, and UTC-split ranges for non-UTC organizers (e.g. PT 9-17 becomes 1020-1439 plus 0-60 next day), wrongly reject valid slots.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:110 — The override-day match compares UTC calendar dates (and uses local-mode dayjs format for the override side), not organizer-local dates, so overrides crossing UTC midnight reject valid in-override slots and block adjacent working-hour slots of the neighbouring local day.

packages/lib/slots.ts:218 — Converting the override to invitee minutes with hour()*60+minute() drops day wrap-around, so overrides that cross invitee midnight get startTime > endTime (all slots dropped), or show up on the wrong calendar day when the shift crosses a day boundary.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:114 — Dayjs objects are compared with ===, which is always false, so the start==end check for an "unavailable all day" override never fires, and a slot starting exactly at that instant falls through as available.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:123 — The override upper bound checks slotStartTime.isAfter(end) instead of slotEndTime, so slots that run past the override end, or start exactly at it, are accepted.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:142 — The working-hours `end` is computed from slotStartTime (same as start) instead of slot end, so slots extending past workingHour.endTime are accepted.

packages/lib/slots.ts:212 — The organizer offset is taken at the fake-UTC override instant, parsed from Date.toString(), with no fallback when override.timeZone is undefined (uses host/browser tz), which gives wrong offsets near DST transitions or for callers without timeZone.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:107 — checkIfIsAvailable runs an Intl-backed dayjs.tz() plus up to ~6 fresh dayjs(date.start/end).add() constructions for every override on every slot for every host (slots x hosts x overrides, e.g. ~3k slots x 10 hosts x 20 overrides = ~600k tz calls, seconds of CPU per request), though the shifted start/end/day-key depend only on the override and user timezone and could be computed once per user before the slot loop

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:106 — find() over dateOverrides returns true only for a matching day where the slot falls outside the override, so on non-override days and on slots inside an override it scans the whole unbounded per-user override list (every historical override, not limited to the requested range) on each slot; a per-user Map keyed by date string would make this O(1)
packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:111 — slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD") is loop-invariant but gets recomputed inside the find callback for every override on every slot

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:513 — The round-robin/loose-host path now pays the full per-override tz scan for each (slot, candidate userId) pair after an O(hosts) looseHostAvailability.find, so cost grows with hosts x slots x overrides; with large round-robin teams it becomes the dominant term

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:579 — userAvailability.find runs for each slot x userId in the selectedSlots branch only to supply organizerTimeZone, but that call passes no dateOverrides, so the timezone is never used and the lookup is wasted work

packages/lib/slots.ts:219 — Each active override builds 4 dayjs().utc().add() chains (start and end each constructed twice for hour() and minute()) plus 2 .tz() conversions that re-parse Date.toString() strings; one conversion per endpoint would do

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:139 — New working-hours gate in checkIfIsAvailable has no tests, so the bug where a slot is rejected if ANY same-day range (e.g. split 9-12/13-17 hours or hours crossing UTC midnight) excludes it goes undetected.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:106 — New date-override gating in checkIfIsAvailable is never exercised by a discriminating test: all asserted slots lie inside the override, so the test passes even if this block is deleted or broken.

apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts:56 — The toHaveTimeSlots matcher iterates actual slots only and never compares lengths, so the new assertion still passes if some or all expected slots are missing (e.g. an empty array or a prefix).
packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:142 — end` is computed from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime, and no test puts a slot past the working-hours end, so the typo is never caught.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:123 — Only slotStart > override end is checked (slotEnd past the override end is allowed), and no test covers slots that straddle or end exactly at the override boundary.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:114 — The zero-length or "unavailable day" override check compares Dayjs objects with ===, which is always false, and no test covers an override that marks a full day unavailable.

packages/lib/slots.ts:219 — Override minutes are taken with .hour()/.minute() after the offset shift, so overrides that cross midnight in the invitee's timezone wrap or collapse, and no test covers negative-offset or far-offset invitees (e.g. America/*, Pacific/Auckland).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:110 — Overrides are matched to slots by UTC calendar date rather than the organizer's local day, and no test uses a negative-offset organizer or an override near local midnight where the two dates differ.

apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts:788 — The new timezone test only covers a +30-minute organizer/invitee difference in one direction and does not cover DST transitions or overrides for team hosts (collective or round-robin) in different timezones.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:585 — organizerTimeZone is passed on the selected-slots path without dateOverrides/workingHours, so it has no effect there, and neither this path nor the seated-event short-circuit is tested alongside the new gating.

apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts:792 — The new Dhaka (+6) test reuses the IST-aligned 18:30Z window instead of the invitee's own midnight (18:00Z), so it does not check day-boundary handling for that timezone.
packages/lib/slots.ts:212 — No test covers an override without timeZone (the field is optional on TimeRange), where .tz(undefined) falls back to the default zone and produces a wrong offset.

goldens.comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime

Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

per_golden_matches.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:133 — When a slot falls on a date-override day and inside its window, `return true` exits before the `busy.every` check, so existing bookings, calendar events and buffers during override hours are ignored and the slot can be double-booked.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the new date-override logic runs before the `busy.every(...)` block. If a slot is on a date-override day and *within* the override window, `dateOverrideExist` is set to `true` and the function immediately `return true;` (see the `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` block). That early return bypasses the subsequent `busy.every` checks for existing bookings/calendar busy times/buffers, allowing a slot to be marked available even if it overlaps `busy` intervals.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:123 — With several override ranges on the same day (e.g. 09-11 and 14-16), every slot is outside at least one range, so `find` returns truthy and every slot on that day is rejected.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the date override check uses `dateOverrides.find(...)` and returns `false` (rejects the slot) if *any* override on the same day determines the slot is outside that override (`slotEndTime <= override.start` or `slotStartTime > override.end`). With multiple override ranges on the same day (e.g. 09–11 and 14–16), a slot within one range (10:00) will still be outside the other range (before 14:00), causing the `find` callback to return `true` for the second override and the slot to be rejected. This matches the reported issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:110 — Overrides are matched to slots by the UTC calendar date, not the organizer's local date, so a PST evening override (e.g. Jan 11 5-8PM = Jan 12 UTC) wipes normal Jan 12 slots and drops override slots that fall after UTC midnight.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, overrides are effectively keyed to the slot’s **UTC** day (`slotStartTime = time.utc(); slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")`). The override “day” comparison uses `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format(...)` where `utcOffset` is derived from `organizerTimeZone` but applied by shifting the instant, not by formatting in the organizer’s timezone (it does not use `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).format(...)`). For a PST evening override (local Jan 11) whose `Date` instant is already Jan 12 UTC, this logic will match `Jan 12` and can cause the override to be treated as applying to the UTC day (wiping normal Jan 12 slots / misclassifying override slots), matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:139 — The new working-hours check returns "outside" if the slot is outside ANY entry for that weekday, so split schedules (lunch breaks) and UTC-midnight-split entries (e.g. Sydney 9-5) reject valid slots.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the new working-hours gate uses `workingHours.find(...)` and returns `false` if it finds *any* `workingHour` for that weekday where `start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime`. With multiple ranges for the same day (split schedules), a slot that is valid in one range but not in another will still match the “outside” predicate for the other range and be rejected. This behavior is directly implied by the `find` + “outside” condition in the diff (and `end` is also incorrectly computed equal to `start`, worsening correctness).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/slots.ts:219 — The override conversion keeps only hour*60+minute after adding the offset, dropping the day, so a window that crosses the invitee's midnight gets endTime < startTime, or lands 24h off (e.g. IST 00:30 override shown to a UTC invitee on the next day); checkIfIsAvailable then rejects those slots, so the override is silently lost.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts` (around the changed override mapping), the computed `startTime`/`endTime` are reduced to “minutes within the day” via `hour() * 60 + minute()` after applying an offset (`dayjs(...).utc().add(offset, "minute")`). This necessarily discards any day rollover caused by the offset. If an override shifts across midnight for the invitee (or spans midnight), `endTime` can become numerically less than `startTime`, and the subsequent logic that “unsets all working hours that relate to this user availability override” operates on these minute-of-day values, likely misapplying or skipping the override window. The diff does not show any handling/splitting for cross-midnight ranges, so the finding’s core defect (day being dropped causing incorrect override application) is supported by the code change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:110 — The left side uses local-mode `dayjs(date.start).format()` (server TZ) while `slotStartTime` is UTC, so matching only works when the server runs in UTC; tests pass in a UTC CI but break on non-UTC hosts.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, `slotStartTime` is explicitly converted to UTC (`const slotStartTime = time.utc()`), but the date-override side uses `dayjs(date.start)` (local-mode, i.e., host/server TZ) before formatting: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format(...) === slotStartTime.format(...)`. Because `dayjs(Date)` interprets the Date in the server’s local timezone when formatting, the day-match logic can differ on non-UTC hosts, making the comparison environment-dependent as the finding describes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:114 — ===` compares two distinct Dayjs objects and is always false, so the "unavailable all day" (start==end) override branch is dead code and a slot starting exactly at that instant is treated as available.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:123 — The bounds check only rejects slotStart > override end, so a slot starting exactly at the override end or running past it is accepted as inside the override (and then skips the busy check).
packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:142 — end` is computed from slotStartTime instead of the slot end time, so a slot that runs past the end of working hours is never caught.

apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts:797 — toHaveTimeSlots only walks the actual slots, so a subset or a truncated result passes; the new test also has no busy booking inside the override, no multi-range override and no invitee behind the organizer, so it misses the P0/P1 bugs.

adjudication.rationale: The claim that `toHaveTimeSlots` “only walks the actual slots” (so subsets/truncated results pass) cannot be verified from the diff because the matcher implementation isn’t shown. The rest of the finding argues the new test doesn’t cover additional scenarios (busy booking inside override, multi-range override, invitee behind organizer), which is true descriptively but is essentially speculative test-scope guidance rather than a diff-demonstrable defect or a specific required coverage gap tied to a newly introduced failure mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:107 — The organizer offset is computed at the fake-UTC wall-clock instant rather than the real instant, so it can be off by an hour on DST transition days.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` (around the new date override logic), a single `utcOffset` is computed from `date.start` via `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1` and then applied to both `date.start` and `date.end` comparisons (`dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")`, etc.). If the override range (or the compared slots) crosses a DST transition, the offset at `date.end` (or at the slot time) can differ by 60 minutes, so using the `date.start` offset for the whole range can misclassify availability by an hour on transition days.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/slots.ts:212 — override.timeZone` is optional; when undefined, `.tz(undefined)` falls back to the server's local timezone, silently giving the wrong offset for callers that don't set it.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts`, the new override adjustment computes `organizerUtcOffset` via `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()`. The diff also makes `timeZone` optional on `TimeRange` (`packages/types/schedule.d.ts`), so `override.timeZone` can be `undefined`. With no guard/default, `.tz(undefined)` can apply an unintended timezone (e.g., local/default), producing an incorrect `offset` and therefore wrong `startTime`/`endTime` minutes for overrides.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:133 — When any date override matches the slot's day, checkIfIsAvailable returns true before the busy check, so bookings and calendar conflicts are ignored on override days (double-booking).

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, after checking date overrides, if a date override exists for the slot’s day (`dateOverrideExist` set inside the `dateOverrides.find` callback), the function immediately returns `true` (`if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }`) before reaching the final `return busy.every(...)` conflict check. This means on any day with a matching override where the slot is within that override window (i.e., not rejected by the earlier `return false` path), calendar/booking conflicts in `busy` are skipped, enabling double-booking.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:106 — dateOverrides.find rejects a slot as soon as one same-day override excludes it, so days with several override ranges (e.g. 9-12 and 14-17) lose valid slots in every range except the first.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the new date override logic does `if (dateOverrides.find((date) => { ... if same-day then dateOverrideExist=true; if slot is before start / after end / start==end return true })) { return false; }`. This means **any** same-day override range that does *not* contain the slot causes an immediate rejection, even if another override range on the same day *does* contain it. With multiple same-day override windows (e.g., 09–12 and 14–17), a slot in 14–17 will be rejected when evaluating the 09–12 override (slotStartTime.isAfter(end) => `return true`), matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:139 — workingHours.find rejects a slot if any entry for that UTC day excludes it, so multiple ranges per day, and UTC-split ranges for non-UTC organizers (e.g. PT 9-17 becomes 1020-1439 plus 0-60 next day), wrongly reject valid slots.

adjudication.rationale: In checkIfIsAvailable, the working-hours gate uses `workingHours.find(...)` to return `false` (reject) if it finds *any* `workingHour` for `slotStartTime.day()` where `start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime` (lines around the added block). This implements “reject if outside any one range” rather than “accept if inside at least one range”. With multiple working-hour ranges on the same day (or split ranges across UTC days), a valid slot inside one range will still be rejected because another range for that day doesn’t contain it. This is a correctness defect visible from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:110 — The override-day match compares UTC calendar dates (and uses local-mode dayjs format for the override side), not organizer-local dates, so overrides crossing UTC midnight reject valid in-override slots and block adjacent working-hour slots of the neighbouring local day.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` the override-day matching is done against `slotStartTime` computed as `time.utc()` (UTC calendar day), while the override side uses `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` where `utcOffset` is derived from `organizerTimeZone` but the `dayjs(date.start)` instance is not created in that timezone. This effectively normalizes overrides toward UTC-day comparisons rather than organizer-local day boundaries, so an override that spans/depends on an organizer-local date boundary (e.g., crossing UTC midnight) can fail to match the intended local day and cause `dateOverrides.find(...)` to treat in-override slots as outside and return `false`. The finding’s description is consistent with the diff logic at the override-day check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/slots.ts:218 — Converting the override to invitee minutes with hour()*60+minute() drops day wrap-around, so overrides that cross invitee midnight get startTime > endTime (all slots dropped), or show up on the wrong calendar day when the shift crosses a day boundary.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts` the new override conversion computes `startTime`/`endTime` as `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 + ...minute()`, i.e., minutes-within-day only. If `add(offset)` shifts the adjusted time across a day boundary (e.g., organizer override 23:30–00:30, or any range that becomes cross-midnight in the invitee TZ), the day component is discarded, so the range can become `startTime > endTime` or be applied to the wrong calendar day when unsetting working hours. The diff shows no handling for wrap-around/overnight ranges, so the finding is a real correctness issue exposed by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:114 — Dayjs objects are compared with ===, which is always false, so the start==end check for an "unavailable all day" override never fires, and a slot starting exactly at that instant falls through as available.
matched_golden_ids: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the same bug: comparing Dayjs instances with === checks object identity rather than the underlying datetime value, so the equality check will not work as intended. The golden adds the fix (.isSame()), while the candidate explains the impact on the "unavailable all day" override logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:123 — The override upper bound checks slotStartTime.isAfter(end) instead of slotEndTime, so slots that run past the override end, or start exactly at it, are accepted.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the date override upper-bound logic only checks `slotStartTime.isAfter(dayjs(date.end)... )` and never compares `slotEndTime` against the override end. This means a slot that starts before the override end but extends past it will not trigger the “outside override” rejection, and a slot starting exactly at `date.end` is also not rejected because `isAfter` is strict (no `isSame` check). The finding matches the added code path in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:142 — The working-hours `end` is computed from slotStartTime (same as start) instead of slot end, so slots extending past workingHour.endTime are accepted.

packages/lib/slots.ts:212 — The organizer offset is taken at the fake-UTC override instant, parsed from Date.toString(), with no fallback when override.timeZone is undefined (uses host/browser tz), which gives wrong offsets near DST transitions or for callers without timeZone.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts`, the new logic computes offsets via `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()` and similarly for `timeZone`. `override.timeZone` is optional (see `packages/types/schedule.d.ts`), and there is no fallback if it is `undefined`, so `dayjs.tz(..., undefined)` will fall back to the runtime/local timezone, producing incorrect offsets for overrides when organizer TZ is missing. Also, parsing via `Date.toString()` is environment-dependent and less reliable than using the `Date` directly (e.g., `dayjs(override.start)`), which can lead to incorrect offset calculations in edge cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:107 — checkIfIsAvailable runs an Intl-backed dayjs.tz() plus up to ~6 fresh dayjs(date.start/end).add() constructions for every override on every slot for every host (slots x hosts x overrides, e.g. ~3k slots x 10 hosts x 20 overrides = ~600k tz calls, seconds of CPU per request), though the shifted start/end/day-key depend only on the override and user timezone and could be computed once per user before the slot loop

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds per-slot date override checks in `checkIfIsAvailable` that repeatedly compute timezone offsets and build multiple Dayjs instances inside `dateOverrides.find(...)` (e.g., `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset()` plus several `dayjs(date.start/end).add(...)` calls) for every slot evaluation. Since `checkIfIsAvailable` is invoked across many slots and potentially per-host schedules, this creates a clear diff-grounded CPU/perf concern; these shifted override values could be precomputed once per override/user timezone rather than recomputed per slot.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:106 — find() over dateOverrides returns true only for a matching day where the slot falls outside the override, so on non-override days and on slots inside an override it scans the whole unbounded per-user override list (every historical override, not limited to the requested range) on each slot; a per-user Map keyed by date string would make this O(1)

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` the new date-override logic uses `dateOverrides.find((date) => { ... })` (around the added block starting near line ~106). The callback only `return true` when the override is on the same day *and* the slot is outside the override window (or `start===end`), otherwise it returns `undefined`. This means on (a) days with no override, and (b) slots that are inside an override window, the `.find()` will scan the entire `dateOverrides` array for every slot checked (O(#slots * #overrides)). The diff does not show any indexing or pre-grouping by date/user, so the performance concern is grounded. The claim that the list is “every historical override, not limited to the requested range” is not fully verifiable from this diff because the DB query/fetch shape isn’t shown here, but the per-slot linear scan issue is real.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:111 — slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD") is loop-invariant but gets recomputed inside the find callback for every override on every slot

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the `dateOverrides.find(...)` callback compares `dayjs(date.start)...format("YYYY MM DD")` to `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")`. Since `slotStartTime` is fixed for the whole `checkIfIsAvailable` call, `slotStartTime.format(...)` is loop-invariant but is recomputed for each override iterated by `find` (and for every slot checked). This is a real, diff-grounded performance inefficiency, not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:513 — The round-robin/loose-host path now pays the full per-override tz scan for each (slot, candidate userId) pair after an O(hosts) looseHostAvailability.find, so cost grows with hosts x slots x overrides; with large round-robin teams it becomes the dominant term

adjudication.rationale: In the loose-host/round-robin filtering path, the diff adds an extra per-candidate lookup and extra per-candidate scanning work. Specifically, for each slot and each `slotUserId`, it now does `userAvailability.find(...)` (O(hosts)) and then calls `checkIfIsAvailable(...)` with `organizerTimeZone` (around the added code near the `slot.userIds.filter(...)`). `checkIfIsAvailable` now performs `dateOverrides.find(...)` with repeated `dayjs.tz(...).utcOffset()` computations and multiple `dayjs(...)` constructions, plus a `workingHours.find(...)` scan, before checking `busy`. This makes runtime grow with slots × candidate users × (dateOverrides + workingHours), which can become dominant for large teams. This is a performance/scale concern evidenced by the new loops, not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:579 — userAvailability.find runs for each slot x userId in the selectedSlots branch only to supply organizerTimeZone, but that call passes no dateOverrides, so the timezone is never used and the lookup is wasted work

adjudication.rationale: In the selectedSlots branch, the call to `checkIfIsAvailable` spreads `...availabilityCheckProps`, which (per the diff) includes `dateOverrides` and `workingHours`. Therefore `organizerTimeZone: userSchedule?.timeZone` can be used by `checkIfIsAvailable` when evaluating `dateOverrides` (it computes an offset from `organizerTimeZone`). The finding’s claim that "that call passes no dateOverrides, so the timezone is never used" is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/slots.ts:219 — Each active override builds 4 dayjs().utc().add() chains (start and end each constructed twice for hour() and minute()) plus 2 .tz() conversions that re-parse Date.toString() strings; one conversion per endpoint would do

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts` the new override mapping does exactly what the finding describes: it computes `organizerUtcOffset` and `inviteeUtcOffset` via `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(...).utcOffset()` (two `.tz()` conversions that re-parse a `Date.toString()`), and then computes `startTime` by calling `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute")` twice (once for `.hour()` and again for `.minute()`), and similarly calls `dayjs(override.end).utc().add(...)` twice for `endTime`. This is an efficiency/performance concern grounded in the diff, not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:139 — New working-hours gate in checkIfIsAvailable has no tests, so the bug where a slot is rejected if ANY same-day range (e.g. split 9-12/13-17 hours or hours crossing UTC midnight) excludes it goes undetected.

adjudication.rationale: The new working-hours gate in `checkIfIsAvailable` is logically incorrect: it uses `workingHours.find(...)` to return `true` when a slot is outside *any* same-day `workingHour` range (`if (start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime) return true;`), which will wrongly reject slots that are inside one split range but outside another on the same day (e.g., 9-12 and 13-17). This is verifiable from the diff. Also, `end` is computed identically to `start` (`const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();`), so it doesn’t represent the slot end at all. The added test only covers date overrides/timezone behavior and does not exercise this working-hours logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:106 — New date-override gating in checkIfIsAvailable is never exercised by a discriminating test: all asserted slots lie inside the override, so the test passes even if this block is deleted or broken.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new filtering logic in `checkIfIsAvailable` (date-override gating and fallback working-hours checks). The only added test (`getSchedule.test.ts`) asserts that a specific set of slots is returned for a timezone-shifted date-override scenario, but it does not (in the shown snippet) assert that any slots *outside* the override window are excluded. If the custom matcher `toHaveTimeSlots` is non-strict (e.g., checks inclusion rather than exact equality), this test would not discriminate failures where the new gating logic is removed/broken. However, strictness of `toHaveTimeSlots` and the surrounding test setup aren’t shown, so this can’t be fully verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts:56 — The toHaveTimeSlots matcher iterates actual slots only and never compares lengths, so the new assertion still passes if some or all expected slots are missing (e.g. an empty array or a prefix).

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows a new test assertion using `toHaveTimeSlots`, but it does not include the implementation of that matcher. The claim that the matcher “iterates actual slots only and never compares lengths,” allowing missing expected slots to pass, cannot be verified from the provided diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:142 — end` is computed from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime, and no test puts a slot past the working-hours end, so the typo is never caught.
matched_golden_ids: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate explicitly states that `end` is computed from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`, which is exactly the golden issue (incorrect end time calculation due to using the start time variable).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:123 — Only slotStart > override end is checked (slotEnd past the override end is allowed), and no test covers slots that straddle or end exactly at the override boundary.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` (new date override logic), the “outside override” checks only handle slots ending before/at `date.start` (`slotEndTime.isBefore/isSame(date.start)`) or slots starting after `date.end` (`slotStartTime.isAfter(date.end)`). There is no check for slots where `slotStartTime` is within the override window but `slotEndTime` extends past `date.end` (i.e., straddling the override end). In that case, `dateOverrideExist` becomes true, the callback returns nothing (so `.find(...)` is falsy), and then `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` marks the slot available even though it exceeds the override. The added test in `getSchedule.test.ts` only covers timezone behavior and does not exercise boundary/straddle cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:114 — The zero-length or "unavailable day" override check compares Dayjs objects with ===, which is always false, and no test covers an override that marks a full day unavailable.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` the new date-override logic contains `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")) { return true; }`, which compares two distinct Dayjs objects by reference, so it will always be false even when start/end represent the same instant. That makes the intended “zero-length / unavailable day” override case ineffective. The added test covers timezone differences but does not cover a zero-length override.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/slots.ts:219 — Override minutes are taken with .hour()/.minute() after the offset shift, so overrides that cross midnight in the invitee's timezone wrap or collapse, and no test covers negative-offset or far-offset invitees (e.g. America/*, Pacific/Auckland).

adjudication.rationale: In packages/lib/slots.ts the new override conversion computes minutes-of-day via `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour()/minute()` (and same for end). This necessarily discards any day rollover caused by the offset shift, so an override that becomes cross-midnight in the invitee timezone could yield `startTime > endTime` or apply to the wrong day unless handled elsewhere. The diff does not show any normalization/splitting for that case. The added test only covers a +6:00 invitee case and does not exercise negative or large offsets that would more readily trigger day rollovers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:110 — Overrides are matched to slots by UTC calendar date rather than the organizer's local day, and no test uses a negative-offset organizer or an override near local midnight where the two dates differ.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` the override/day match is done by comparing `slotStartTime = time.utc()`’s calendar date (`slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")`) against an adjusted `date.start` (`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format(...)`). This is still fundamentally keyed off the slot’s UTC day rather than computing the organizer-local day for the slot (no `slotStartTime.tz(organizerTimeZone)` comparison). The newly added test only covers a positive-offset (+6:00) scenario and does not exercise a negative-offset organizer (or an override near local midnight where organizer-local date and UTC date can diverge), so this edge case remains untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts:788 — The new timezone test only covers a +30-minute organizer/invitee difference in one direction and does not cover DST transitions or overrides for team hosts (collective or round-robin) in different timezones.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a single new test case in `apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts` that exercises `getSchedule` with an invitee `timeZone: Timezones["+6:00"]` and asserts returned UTC slots, but it does not add coverage for other nontrivial scenarios implicated by the new timezone/override logic (e.g., DST boundary behavior or multi-host/team scheduling paths). The PR also modifies availability logic in multiple places (`packages/lib/slots.ts` offset math and `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts` dateOverrides/workingHours checks with `organizerTimeZone`), yet the added test only validates one direction/case. The specific “+30-minute difference” detail is not verifiable from the shown diff, but the broader point about limited coverage is grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:585 — organizerTimeZone is passed on the selected-slots path without dateOverrides/workingHours, so it has no effect there, and neither this path nor the seated-event short-circuit is tested alongside the new gating.

adjudication.rationale: In the shown diff, the “selected-slots”/per-user filtering path calls `checkIfIsAvailable({ time: slot.time, busy, ...availabilityCheckProps, organizerTimeZone: userSchedule?.timeZone })`, i.e. it *does* spread `availabilityCheckProps` (which is the shared bundle intended for availability checks). The finding’s claim that `organizerTimeZone` is passed there “without dateOverrides/workingHours” is not supported by the diff. The testing claim (“neither this path nor the seated-event short-circuit is tested”) cannot be verified from the diff alone because existing tests outside the added snippet may already cover those paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts:792 — The new Dhaka (+6) test reuses the IST-aligned 18:30Z window instead of the invitee's own midnight (18:00Z), so it does not check day-boundary handling for that timezone.

adjudication.rationale: The added test for `Timezones["+6:00"]` uses `startTime: `${plus1DateString}T18:30:00.000Z`` and `endTime: `${plus2DateString}T18:29:59.999Z``, which is the same 18:30Z/18:29:59Z window as the prior IST-style case. For a +6:00 invitee, the local midnight boundary corresponds to 18:00Z, so this test window starts at 00:30 local (not 00:00) and therefore does not specifically exercise the edge case of a date override aligned to local midnight for that timezone. This is a test adequacy/coverage issue, not a verifiable runtime defect in the diffed logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/slots.ts:212 — No test covers an override without timeZone (the field is optional on TimeRange), where .tz(undefined) falls back to the default zone and produces a wrong offset.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts` the new logic uses `override.timeZone` directly: `dayjs(...).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()` without a fallback/guard (lines around the changed block). The diff also makes `TimeRange.timeZone` optional (`packages/types/schedule.d.ts`), so an override without `timeZone` is a plausible edge case. However, in this PR’s main construction path, `getSchedule` now maps `availability.dateOverrides` to include `timeZone: availability.timeZone`, so the diff itself doesn’t show an actual failing runtime path—only that the code would behave differently if `timeZone` were missing. That makes this primarily an uncovered edge-case / missing-test concern tied to the new timezone-offset logic, not a verifiable defect from the diff alone.
